'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Communal conflicts in Nigeria]]
**[[Fulani]] herdsmen attack the community of Odugbeho in [[Agatu]], [[Benue State]], killing 40 civilians in the process. [http://saharareporters.com/2021/06/07/fulani-herdsmen-strike-benue-community-again-kill-40-residents (''Sahara Reporters'')]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Alphabet Inc.]], [[parent company]] of [[Google]], announces that it has settled an [[antitrust]] suit with the [[France|French]] ''[[Autorité de la concurrence]]'' with a payment of [[Euro|€]]220m ([[US$]]270 million). The settlement amounts to less than 0.7% of Alphabet Inc.'s yearly earnings. [https://www.bbc.com/news/business-57383867 (BBC News)] [https://www.nytimes.com/live/2021/06/07/business/economy-stock-market-news (''The New York Times'')]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2021 Ghotki rail crash]]
**Two [[passenger train]]s [[train wreck|collide]] in [[Ghotki District|Ghotki]], [[Sindh]], [[Pakistan]], killing 40 people and injuring nearly 120 others. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-57380615 (BBC News)]
*[[June 2021 Pune fire]]
**At least 18 people are killed in a fire at a [[chemical plant]] in [[Pune]], [[Maharashtra]], [[India]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-india-57395290 (BBC News)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Philippines]]
****[[COVID-19 vaccination in the Philippines]]
*****The Philippines begins the mass vaccination campaign for economic frontline workers. [https://www.rappler.com/nation/philippines-covid-19-vaccination-economic-frontline-workers-begins-june-2021 (Rappler)]
****The Philippines's [[Food and Drug Administration (Philippines)|Food and Drug Administration]] approves for [[Emergency Use Authorization|emergency use]] the [[BBIBP-CorV|Sinopharm BBIBP-CorV vaccine]]. [https://www.rappler.com/nation/fda-grants-emergency-use-approval-sinopharm-covid-19-vaccines (Rappler)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Taiwan]]
****[[Taiwan]] extends its nationwide alert level 3 until June 28 as the number of [[COVID-19]] cases continues to remain high. [https://focustaiwan.tw/society/202106070005 (Focus Taiwan)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Thailand]]
****[[Thailand]] begins a long-awaited mass vaccination campaign against COVID-19 which aims to inoculate 70% of its population by the end of this year in order to prepare for a wider reopening next year. [https://www.straitstimes.com/asia/se-asia/thailand-begins-mass-covid-19-vaccine-rollout-as-tourism-reopening-looms (''The Straits Times'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Malta]]
****[[Malta]] reports no new cases of COVID-19 for the first time since July 25, 2020, as bars, cinemas and theatres are reopened following months of closures. [https://www.maltatoday.com.mt/news/national/110105/malta_records_no_new_covid19_cases_for_the_first_time_in_almost_11_months_ (''Malta Today'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Spain]]
****[[Spain]] reopens its international borders to travellers who have been [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccinated]] against COVID-19. For [[tourism in Spain|tourists]] from low-risk countries, no proof of [[vaccination]], recovery, or diagnostic [[COVID-19 testing|test]] will be required and [[antigen]] tests are now accepted for travellers from risk zone countries. [https://english.elpais.com/society/2021-06-07/spain-reopens-to-global-tourists-provided-they-can-prove-they-have-been-vaccinated-against-covid-19.html (''El País'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Cook Islands]]
***The [[Cook Islands]] reports the country's first positive case of COVID-19. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/444190/cook-islands-detects-historical-covid-19-case (RNZ International)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Uganda]]
***[[President of Uganda|President]] [[Yoweri Museveni]] reimposes a [[COVID-19 lockdowns|lockdown]] including the closure of all educational institutions, the shutdown of weekly open markets, suspension of some inter-city travel, and the suspension of church services following an increase in the number of [[COVID-19]] cases. [https://www.usnews.com/news/world/articles/2021-06-06/uganda-re-imposes-lockdown-to-beat-back-covid-19-case-surge (U.S. News & World Report)]
*The [[Food and Drug Administration|U.S. Food and Drug Administration]] approves the use of [[aducanumab]] to treat [[Alzheimer's disease]], the first Alzheimer's drug to be approved in 18 years and the first to target the disease process. The drug is considered controversial as [[clinical trial]]s gave conflicting results on its effectiveness. [https://www.nytimes.com/2021/06/07/health/aduhelm-fda-alzheimers-drug.html (''The New York Times'')] [https://www.bbc.com/news/health-57383763 (BBC News)]

'''International relations'''
*[[U.S.-Mexico border crisis]]
**In [[Guatemala]], [[Vice President of the United States|U.S. Vice President]] [[Kamala Harris]] announces several steps to address the migration crisis at the [[Northern Triangle of Central America|Northern Triangle]] during a joint conference with [[President of Guatemala|Guatemalan President]] [[Alejandro Giammattei]]. She also urged migrants not to flee to the [[Mexico–United States border]]. [https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/white-house/harris-guatemala-warns-potential-migrants-do-not-come-n1269892 (NBC News)]
*[[President of Russia|Russian President]] [[Vladimir Putin]] signs a law formalizing [[Russia]]'s withdrawal from the [[Treaty on Open Skies]]. [https://www.msn.com/en-us/news/world/update-1-putin-signs-law-taking-russia-out-of-open-skies-arms-control-treaty/ar-AAKMwci?ocid=BingNews (MSN)]
*[[Maldives|Maldivian]] Minister of Foreign Affairs [[Abdulla Shahid]] is elected the 76th [[President of the United Nations General Assembly]]. [https://indianexpress.com/article/world/maldives-abdulla-shahid-elected-as-president-of-the-76th-session-of-unga-7348425/ (''The Indian Express'')]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[2021 Israel–Palestine crisis]]
**A pro-[[Israeli settlement|settler]] march that was scheduled for Thursday and would have traveled through sensitive sites in [[East Jerusalem]] is canceled after [[Israeli police]] refused to authorize it. However, the police said they would review a petition calling for the march to be rescheduled. The cancellation follows a warning from [[Hamas]] senior leader [[Khalil al-Hayya]] that the march could lead to renewed violence. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/6/7/police-ban-a-planned-controversial-far-right-jerusalem-march (Al Jazeera English)]
**[[Attorney General of Israel]] [[Avichai Mandelblit]] tells the [[Supreme Court of Israel|Supreme Court]] he will not intervene in the [[Sheikh Jarrah property dispute|Sheikh Jarrah case]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/6/7/israeli-attorney-general-will-not-intervene-in-sheikh-jarrah-case (Al Jazeera English)]
*[[Immigration detention in Australia]]
**The [[Federal Court of Australia]] finds an [[Iraqis in Australia|Iraqi]] [[asylum seeker]] detained for over two years was unlawfully imprisoned and orders the [[Australian Government|Commonwealth government]] to pay him [[AU$]]350,000 in damages. The case is expected to set a precedent for [[Refugee law|refugee rights]] claims in the future. [https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/2021/jun/07/australian-government-ordered-to-pay-iraqi-asylum-seeker-350000-for-over-two-years-of-unlawful-detention (''The Guardian'')]
*[[LGBT rights in India]]
**The [[Madras High Court]] orders "strict action" to be taken against individuals that promote [[conversion therapy]], and issues guidelines to [[Law enforcement in India|the police]], [[Education in India|education institutes]], and [[Judiciary of India|the judiciary]] on how to address LGBT issues and individuals. [https://scroll.in/latest/996919/madras-hc-bans-cure-of-sexual-orientation-issues-guidelines-to-police-to-handle-lgbtq-cases (''Scroll.in'')] 
*[[Donald Trump sexual misconduct allegations]]
**The [[United States Justice Department|U.S. Justice Department]] announces it will defend former [[President of the United States|President]] [[Donald Trump]] in a [[United States defamation law|defamation]] suit brought against him by [[E. Jean Carroll]], who says Trump [[Rape in the United States|raped]] her in the 1990s. [https://www.wsj.com/articles/justice-department-to-defend-trump-in-lawsuit-over-rape-claim-11623129987 (''The Wall Street Journal'')]
*Russian oppositional leader [[Alexei Navalny]] is returned to prison after fully recovering from his [[hunger strike]]. [https://www.dw.com/en/alexei-navalny-returns-to-prison-after-hunger-strike/a-57799841 (Deutsche Welle)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2021 Mexican legislative election]]
**The [[Instituto Nacional Electoral|National Electoral Institute]] reports that [[President of Mexico|President]] [[Andrés Manuel López Obrador]]'s coalition [[Juntos Hacemos Historia]] is projected to win between 265 and 292 seats in the [[Chamber of Deputies (Mexico)|Chamber of Deputies]], retaining its majority but without the [[supermajority|two-thirds majority]] that it previously had. His party [[National Regeneration Movement]] (MORENA) saw losses in [[Mexico City]], previously a MORENA stronghold. López Obrador subsequently vows to do more to help the poor. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/mexican-president-keeps-congress-loses-shine-mid-term-vote-2021-06-07/ (Reuters)]
*[[2021 Malian coup d'état]]
**[[Assimi Goïta]] is sworn-in as [[List of heads of state of Mali|President of Mali]] after the recent coup d'état, which was considered a "[[Coup d'état|coup]] within a coup" after Goïta, who directed the [[2020 Malian coup d'état|2020 coup]], carried out another coup and arrested the leaders that were in charge after the 2020 coup. [https://www.dw.com/en/mali-assimi-goita-sworn-in-as-transitional-president/a-57798691 (Deutsche Welle)]
*[[2021 Haitian constitutional referendum]]
**[[President of Haiti|President]] [[Jovenel Moïse]] postpones the constitutional referendum, originally scheduled for June 27, to an unknown date citing [[COVID-19 pandemic in Haiti|rising COVID-19 cases]] in [[Haiti|the country]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/6/8/haiti-postpones-june-27-constitutional-referendum (Al Jazeera English)]
